Article Title: LinkedIn cofounder Reid Hoffman defends AI datacenters; his advice to tech companies ‘make sure the…’
Article Text:
Reid Hoffman

Escalating debate over infrastructure costs

As the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence (AI) data centres faces growing scrutiny across America, LinkedIn co-founder Reid Hoffman is pushing back against critics, arguing that the massive wave of datacenter construction is keeping the US economy afloat. He said that it is the responsibility of the tech companies building the infrastructure to ensure there are no problems faced by nearby residents. Speaking on the Newcomer podcast recently, he gave advice to tech giants to address mounting neighbourhood pushback directly while pointing to the immediate macroeconomic boost.“Make sure the local community gets a sustainable benefit. Make sure noise, the environment, and everything else is taken care of. Make sure electricity prices stay the same or go down. And then allow the local community to say, ‘I want it, I don’t want it,’ and exercise their right to self-determination," he said, outlining clear conditions that developers must satisfy before moving forward with new builds.The rush to construct facilities capable of training and running advanced AI models has ignited both political and social resistance across the US due to increased strain on power grids and drinking water supply.Data centres require tremendous amounts of power to run and cool high-density servers, sparking fears of strained regional power grids and higher residential utility bills. Similarly, heavy cooling requirements have raised persistent worries over the strain placed on local water supplies, alongside concerns over persistent facility noise.While the initial building phase drives demand for skilled trades like electricians and carpenters, completed datacenters require relatively few permanent operational workers on-site. Hoffman, however, defended the record capital flowing into AI facilities, claiming the investments deliver wide-reaching economic benefits far beyond Silicon Valley balance sheets.“All of this capital infusion, people think, ‘Oh, that’s just going to tech companies’ (...) but a massive percentage of it is going toward data center construction, which means construction electricians, carpenters, real estate development, and so on (...) and because of that, that capital is the only reason we’re not in a recession,” Hoffman said.Some tech giants announced their quarterly earnings, suggesting that there is no slowdown in capital expenditure when it comes to infrastructure spending. Google-parent Alphabet lost $500 billion in market value post announcements after it held its guidance at $195 billion to $205 billion.
Article Summary: LinkedIn co-founder Reid Hoffman says datacenter construction is keeping the US economy afloat. He said it is the responsibility of tech companies building the infrastructure to ensure there are no problems faced by nearby residents. The rush to construct facilities capable of training and running advanced AI models has ignited both political and social resistance.

Article Title: Reed Jobs, who lost his father Steve Jobs to cancer, has taken how to fight the disease as his life's work, now he sees a common anti-obesity drug bringing a revolution
Article Text:
Reed Jobs, who lost his father Steve Jobs to cancer, has taken how to fight the disease as his life's work, now he sees a common anti-obesity drug bringing a revolution

A personal mission born from his father's diagnosis

Why Reed Jobs is betting on GLP-1 drugs

Comparing obesity to smoking

Research suggests potential Cancer benefits

A different vision of victory against cancer

Reed Jobs, the son of Apple founder Steve Jobs , has made the fight against cancer a central mission of his life after losing his father to pancreatic cancer. That path led him to start Yosemite, an oncology-focused venture capital firm. Now, the founder of an oncology-focused venture capital firm, he believes that a class of anti-obesity drugs known as GLP-1s could play a major role in preventing cancer and other chronic diseases. According to a Fortune report, Jobs described the medicines as some of "the most impactful drugs that we've ever made." Jobs says the firm’s second fund has passed its $350 million target.After Steve Jobs was diagnosed with pancreatic cancer in 2003, Reed Jobs started working in cancer research laboratories and later studied pre-med at Stanford University, determined to help find better ways to combat the disease. This journey eventually led Jobs to start Yosemite, which is an investment focused firm which exclusively works on oncology. Speaking to Fortune's Term Sheet, Jobs mentioned that the company’s second funding round has already exceeded its target $350 million, reflecting growing investor interest in cancer-related innovation.In a recent Term Sheet interview with Fortune’s Allie Garfinkle, Jobs said he is excited about experimental cancer vaccines, but also about GLP-1 drugs, the class of medicines widely used for weight loss.He calls them among the most impactful drugs ever made. In his view, they will help people who are obese and struggling with it, and will also affect cancer, cardiovascular disease and many other conditions.His argument is that GLP-1s could help prevent cancer by cutting obesity, which the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) links to a higher risk of 13 types of cancer. The CDC estimates that obesity-associated cancers make up 40 percent of all cancers diagnosed in the US each year, including colon, pancreatic, kidney and breast cancer.Jobs compared obesity to smoking, saying the longer someone lives with either risk factor, the greater their chances of developing certain cancers. A 2024 study cited by Fortune found that smoking caused an estimated 19.3 percent of US cancer cases, compared with 7.6 percent linked to excess body weight. He said GLP-1s are a fantastic way for obese people to stop being obese very quickly.“The more time you spend being obese, the greater your odds of getting an obesity-related disease are,” he said. “[GLP-1s] are a fantastic way for obese people to basically stop being obese very quickly.”Some scientific studies have begun to explore whether the benefits of GLP-1 drugs extend beyond weight loss. Jobs pointed to growing evidence that reducing obesity may also lower cancer risk. A study published in JAMA Oncology in 2025 followed more than 86,000 adults eligible for anti-obesity medications and found that patients taking GLP-1 drugs had a 17% lower risk of developing the cancers examined in the study compared with non-users. Jobs acknowledged that the medications are not without drawbacks, including concerns about muscle loss, but argued that their emergence represents one of biotechnology's biggest breakthroughs in recent years.Despite advancement in the cancer research, Jobs revealed that he does not believe that humanity will ever be able to eliminate the disease completely. This is because the human cells can always mutate and become cancerous, and he feels that total eradication is an unrealistic goal. However, he hopes that cancer can eventually be managed in a similar way as HIV, where the patients can live a long and healthy life with the help of ongoing treatment. “It’s the victory over death, and that is what I want for cancer patients, and I think that that’s more achievable and more realistic,” Jobs said.
Article Summary: Reed Jobs, the son of Apple founder Steve Jobs, has made the fight against cancer a central mission of his life after losing his father to pancreatic cancer. Now, the founder of an oncology-focused venture capital firm, he believes a class of anti-obesity drugs known as GLP-1s could play a major role in preventing cancer.

Article Title: MacKenzie Scott and Melinda French Gates, billionaire Brian Armstrong does not agree with your kind of donations and philanthropy; says: My main fear is ...
Article Text:
MacKenzie Scott

Why Brian Armstrong is sceptical of traditional philanthropy

How Brian Armstrong's view differs from other billionaires

Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong views billionaire philanthropy differently from MacKenzie Scott and Melinda French Gates. While Jeff Bezos’ ex-wife has donated more than $26 billion to nearly 2,700 organisations since 2019 and Bill Gates’ former wife has directed hundreds of millions of dollars towards causes including women's health, Armstrong says many charities can end up having a negative impact on society. Armstrong shared his views on a recently released episode of the Katie Miller podcast. His main concern about forming a foundation, he said, is that someone could someday hijack it for an ideology he doesn’t align with.“The biggest fear with starting a foundation is that it just gets captured by some ideology [and] that I lose control of it,” Armstrong said. He compared it to the Ford Foundation, saying that Henry Ford would be “turning over in his grave” if he knew what the organisation was doing.“The common view is that philanthropy is like this noble cause,” said Armstrong. “I guess I have sort of a contrarian view, which is like a lot of charities and philanthropies are actually net negative on the world, and they get captured.”​Armstrong said it is “remarkably hard to find” a philanthropic organisation that has not been captured by ideology or produced unintended consequences. He gave the example of a hypothetical nonprofit focused on criminal justice reform that could ultimately “just increased crime.”​He said he has a donor-advised fund, or DAF, that lets him set aside money for charitable giving and decide later where the funds should go. “And I just try to put money toward things that I think are helping civilisation advance,” Armstrong said, though he didn't specify which causes he currently supports.​He didn’t rule out establishing a foundation in the future, but he thinks it is “crazy” to do it now. His desire for a DAF is part of his broader goal of retaining control over how his charitable money is spent.MacKenzie Scott has chosen another route. She donated $7.2 billion last year alone through her Yield Giving initiative, and her grants to historically Black institutions have pushed her total donations in this field past $1 billion.She has also recently donated $60 million to Global Methane Hub and $20 million to Active Minds. Forbes has ranked MacKenzie Scott as the third most generous philanthropist alive, with around 46% of her net worth already donated.​Likewise, Melinda French Gates has criticised the rate at which billionaires distribute their money, but here her disappointment centres on how philanthropy works, not charity itself. In late 2025, she said the Giving Pledge had failed in its mission because too little of billionaires' wealth reached those it was meant to help.Other wealthy entrepreneurs have expressed concerns similar to Armstrong's. Elon Musk has complained about the difficulty of giving money away effectively and criticised Scott's philanthropy, arguing that it was making the world a “worse place.”Peter Thiel, the PayPal cofounder and venture capitalist, has also questioned the Giving Pledge, saying it had “really run out of energy.” He has said he discouraged people from signing it and encouraged existing signatories to withdraw.
Article Summary: Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong is sceptical of traditional philanthropy. His main concern about forming a foundation is that someone could hijack it for an ideology he doesn't align with. MacKenzie Scott has donated more than $26 billion to nearly 2,700 organisations since 2019.

Article Title: Intel stock sees worst fall since 1970, plant shutdown in Israel hurt, US government loses billions
Article Text:
Representative Image

Israel plant explosion disrupts chip shipments

Revenue and earnings forecasts miss expectations

“We see the PC slowdown continuing at least through the first half of next year,”

“We will continue making disciplined investments in capacity and working capital to increase supply and support future growth.”

“Not fixed yet.”

US government and Nvidia stakes lose value

“We’re going to have a couple of customers ready to announce the next two quarters,”

Intel shares fell 28.58% on Friday to $65.76. The decline followed a weaker-than-expected forecast that reflected an extended shutdown at a chip plant in Israel and continued weakness in the personal computer market. According to CNBC, the stock was headed for its worst day since 1974 and its second-steepest decline on record.The sell-off erased about $12 billion from the value of the US government’s stake, although the investment remained profitable, the report said. It also marked a setback for chief executive Lip-Bu Tan’s turnaround effort after Intel shares had gained about 150% this year before the company’s latest earnings report. The company expects the Israel disruption alone to cost approximately $600 million in revenue over two quarters.Intel’s forecast accounts for an explosion at an Israeli fabrication plant that killed two workers and seriously injured a third earlier in October. Tan described the incident as an “unfortunate and tragic accident” and said it caused an “extended shutdown” affecting shipments of 10-nanometre chips.Intel’s finance chief, David Zinsner, said the lost revenue would total about $600 million over two quarters. The disruption adds to pressure from a slowing PC market, where rising costs for memory and other components are affecting demand. Global PC shipments fell 4% in the second quarter versus a year earlier, according to Counterpoint Research.Intel forecast revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion for the current quarter, below analysts’ expectations of $17.1 billion, according to LSEG. The company also projected adjusted earnings of 25 cents per share, below analysts' 43 cents per share. Adjusted earnings exclude certain items from the company’s reported results.Zinsner said.DA Davidson analysts downgraded Intel to neutral from buy in a report titledThey acknowledged industry-wide PC weakness but questioned whether the company’s valuation was justified.The Trump administration led the US government into taking a 10% stake in Intel more than a year ago. CNBC reported that Friday’s decline reduced its value by about $12 billion without eliminating the investment’s overall gain. Nvidia’s Intel stake also fell by about $6 billion.Tan’s recovery plan includes expanding Intel’s foundry business, which manufactures chips for other companies. Intel is producing its advanced 18A technology at high volume in Arizona, but the report said it still had no external customers for its new chips.Tan said on the earnings call.
Article Summary: Intel shares fell 28.58% on Friday to $65.76. The stock was headed for its worst day since 1974 and its second-steepest decline on record. The sell-off erased about $12 billion from the value of the US government’s stake.

Article Title: Google sees its worst day in 20 years, but why it may not be alone
Article Text:
Google-parent Alphabet sees its worst day in 20 years, but why it may not be alone

Why did Google 's stock suffer its worst fall in 20 years

Why Google's AI spending concerns may not be limited to Alphabet

Amazon, Meta are also facing AI spending scrutiny

Google-parent Alphabet witnessed its worst stock market performance in more than 20 years on Thursday, October 29. The company’s shares plunged 12.6% following its latest earnings report. The decline wiped out around $500 billion in Alphabet's market value. Announcing the Q3 results, Alphabet said that it burned through more cash during the quarter, according to a measure called free cash flow, after its purchases of property and equipment topped $51 billion. However, the company may not be alone in facing investor concerns, as the massive cost of building AI infrastructure is putting pressure on the cash flow of major technology companies. Other tech giants, including Microsoft, Amazon, Meta and Oracle, are also committing billions of dollars to AI development, data centres and computing infrastructure.Alphabet's Class A shares fell 12.6% on October 29, marking their worst single-day decline since they began trading more than two decades ago. The fall came after the company reported weaker-than-expected growth for the summer quarter, adding to concerns over its rising AI expenditure.According to the Associated Press, Alphabet's purchases of property and equipment crossed $51 billion during the latest quarter, while its free cash flow turned negative. Free cash flow refers to the money a company has left after paying for its operating expenses and capital investments. It is an important measure of how much cash a business can generate after funding its expansion.The concern is not limited to how much Google is spending, but also how quickly it can recover that money through its AI and cloud businesses. With major technology companies racing to build data centres and secure AI computing capacity, investors are increasingly looking at whether the returns from these investments can keep pace with the rising costs.As mentioned above, Alphabet is not the only technology company spending heavily to build AI infrastructure. Microsoft, Amazon, Meta and Oracle are also investing billions of dollars in data centres, servers, chips and cloud computing capacity to support their AI ambitions.A Reuters analysis published in July found that five major cloud infrastructure companies, Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta and Oracle, could collectively spend more on capital expenditure than they generate in free cash flow by 2027, based on LSEG consensus estimates. The analysis estimated that their combined capital expenditure could increase by around $534 billion between 2025 and 2027, while their annual operating cash flow could rise by approximately $340 billion over the same period.This highlights the financial pressure that could emerge as companies continue expanding their AI infrastructure. Even when AI-related revenue grows, the cost of building and maintaining the infrastructure needed to support these services could consume a significant portion of the cash generated by their businesses.Amazon is among the biggest spenders in the AI infrastructure race. The company said it remains on track to spend around $220 billion on capital expenditure in 2026, with a significant portion directed towards AI infrastructure. CEO Andy Jassy has defended the investment, saying spending on Amazon Web Services is delivering growth.Meta has also faced investor concerns over its AI expenditure. The company recently raised its 2026 capital expenditure outlook to between $135 billion and $145 billion. Its increased spending outlook overshadowed stronger-than-expected revenue growth, highlighting investor concerns about how quickly its AI investments will translate into financial returns.
Article Summary: Alphabet's Class A shares fell 12.6% on October 29, marking their worst single- day decline since they began trading more than two decades ago. The fall came after the company reported weaker-than-expected growth for the summer quarter, adding to concerns over its rising AI expenditure. Microsoft, Amazon, Meta and Oracle are also investing billions of dollars in data centres, servers, chips and cloud computing capacity.

Article Title: Oracle's Project Jupiter has investors and lenders anxious; company says: We're actually not too worried about what we're...
Article Text:
Oracle calls Jupiter one of 30-40 data centres in the works

Project Jupiter's power plan is still waiting on approvals

Oracle's investors want answers on its data centre spending

Oracle is brushing off the growing worries around Project Jupiter, its $165 billion AI data centre campus in New Mexico. Speaking at Oracle AI World in Las Vegas on October 27, Mahesh Thiagarajan, Oracle's president of Cloud Infrastructure, said, "We're actually not too worried about what we're doing because I think we're building global infrastructure. " He also played down the project's weight, calling it just one of the 30 to 40 data centre projects Oracle has in development each quarter.The calm comes at a tense moment. Last month, Oracle sent a force majeure notice to a unit of Blue Owl Capital, which owns the project's developer, STACK Infrastructure. The notice preserves Oracle's right to delay rent by up to three years if power problems keep the campus from opening on time in 2028. The roughly $18 billion construction loan behind the site has since traded at stressed levels, and Oracle shares are down more than 30% this year.Located near Santa Teresa in Doña Ana County, the 1,400-acre campus is one of the flagship Stargate sites being built for OpenAI. The buildings are going up. The power to run them is yet to be cleared.Jupiter is designed to draw up to 2.45 gigawatts from a private microgrid of Bloom Energy fuel cells running on natural gas.Oracle moved to fuel cells from gas turbines in April, a switch it says cuts nitrogen oxide emissions by about 92%.The approvals have moved slowly. The New Mexico Supreme Court paused the air quality permit process in August before lifting the stay in September, and a permitting hearing is now scheduled for December 7 in Sunland Park. The Green Chile pipeline that would supply the gas still needs federal authorisation, and its start date has slipped to February 2027. The state Land Office has also cancelled rights-of-way for parts of the pipeline route.Oracle maintains the project is on schedule and has called force majeure notices commonplace for developments of this size. Thiagarajan had told county commissioners in July that the campus could turn to the grid if the permit doesn't come through.Under the lease, securing power is Oracle's responsibility, and the company covers the project's debt costs. That leaves Oracle carrying much of the risk at a time when it has taken on about $125 billion in debt to fund its data centre build-out.Oracle, meanwhile, is pitching Jupiter as an economic boost for New Mexico. Earlier this month, the company said the campus is projected to generate more than $13 billion in economic impact and support over 3,100 jobs in the county once fully operational. So far, 1,230 New Mexico residents have worked on the site.Investors will now look to Oracle's upcoming investor day for clarity. Bank of America analysts expect updates on the company's major data centre projects, along with signs of whether Oracle can back its fiscal 2030 revenue targets as the cost of capital rises.Thiagarajan's comments came on the same day Oracle expanded its collaboration with OpenAI, bringing ChatGPT and Codex into its applications.
Article Summary: Jupiter is designed to draw up to 2.45 gigawatts from a private microgrid of Bloom Energy fuel cells running on natural gas. The New Mexico Supreme Court paused the air quality permit process in August before lifting the stay in September. A permitting hearing is now scheduled for December 7 in Sunland Park.

Article Title: Chinese parents sue OpenAI over their daughter's death; say ChatGPT-maker could have prevented her death by making medical advice off-limits
Article Text:
Chinese parents sue OpenAI over their daughter's death; say ChatGPT-maker could have prevented her death by making medical advice off-limits

Lawsuit alleges ChatGPT advised her to reduce medication

Parents claim ChatGPT failed to recognise warning signs

Family calls for stricter limits on medical advice

What OpenAI says

Parents of a 31-year-old Chinese woman who worked as a software engineer at Amazon have reportedly sued OpenAI , alleging that ChatGPT encouraged their daughter to reduce her epilepsy medication without medical supervision before her death in February. The lawsuit claims the company could have prevented her death by making medical advice off-limits to its chatbot. According to a report by The New York Times, the lawsuit was filed by Qun Wan and Meiqin Xu over the death of their daughter, Bowen Wan. The complaint alleges that ChatGPT helped her plan a gradual reduction in her seizure medication and advised her not to tell her doctors about it.The case involves GPT-4o, an older version of ChatGPT that OpenAI removed from the service on February 13, a day after Wan died, according to the report. OpenAI described the case as “incredibly heartbreaking” and said newer models are better at recognising situations that require urgent attention.Bowen Wan had epilepsy and was taking lamotrigine, a medication that had reduced her seizures to a few episodes a month. In January 2026, she reportedly asked ChatGPT about lowering her daily dose because she feared the medication was affecting her speech and could hurt her chances in job interviews.The lawsuit alleges that the chatbot created schedules to reduce her dose to zero within weeks. It also claims that ChatGPT encouraged her to keep the plan from her doctors and supported her decision not to take a blood test that could have measured her medication levels.The report said Wan had also raised concerns about her medication in connection with her green-card application. According to the lawsuit, ChatGPT discussed how a lower dose might affect the medical examination required for the application.Dr. Nicholas Poolos, Wan’s neurologist, told The New York Times that he would not have recommended stopping the medication given her medical history.“No, not rational, no way,” he said. “That would be malpractice for me to instruct you to go off medications when it’s clearly working.”The lawsuit against OpenAI alleges that Wan continued to report symptoms, including confusion, memory gaps and unusual sensations, while reducing her medication. ChatGPT reportedly reassured her that these experiences were part of her brain adjusting to the changes.The New York Times said it reviewed more than 270,000 messages between Wan and ChatGPT. According to the report, she expressed concern about reducing her medication at least 158 times.In her final message to the chatbot on February 11, according to the complaint, Wan asked whether the pain in her head was similar to pain caused by a fever. The chatbot reportedly described the pain as “not dangerous” and said it was part of the recovery process.Her parents, who were in China, asked acquaintances to check on her. They found her body three days later. A postmortem test found a lamotrigine level of 0.64 micrograms per millilitre, about one-fifth of the lower end of the drug’s therapeutic range, the report said.Bowen Wan’s parents argue that OpenAI could have helped prevent her death by making medical advice a restricted category that the chatbot cannot provide, rather than allowing users to override the guidance.They point to OpenAI’s Model Spec, which sets out how its AI models should behave. The lawsuit argues that medical advice about prescription medication should have stronger restrictions, similar to the company’s firm rules in other areas.The case adds to a series of lawsuits alleging that ChatGPT encouraged users to rely on the chatbot instead of seeking support from people around them. In a separate case filed in 2025, the parents of a 16-year-old boy alleged that OpenAI prioritised user engagement over safety.OpenAI said the case involved an older version of ChatGPT and that newer models are better at identifying situations that require urgent attention. The company described the case as “incredibly heartbreaking”.Wan began using ChatGPT in 2023 for relationship advice and help with insurance and disability benefits. By 2025, she was reportedly sending more than 1,500 messages a week to the chatbot and speaking less frequently with her parents.Her parents told The New York Times that the messages were difficult to reconcile with the daughter they knew.“She’s not usually like this,” Xu said. “It’s like she was under a spell.”
Article Summary: Bowen Wan had epilepsy and was taking lamotrigine, a medication that had reduced her seizures to a few episodes a month. In January 2026, she reportedly asked ChatGPT about lowering her daily dose because she feared the medication was affecting her speech and could hurt her chances in job interviews. The lawsuit alleges that the chatbot created schedules to reduce her dose to zero within weeks and encouraged her to keep the plan from her doctors.

Article Title: Google just announced Genie 4: Here’s what it can do, from building walk-through worlds out of a sentence to filling them with sound and speech, and when you might get to try it
Article Text:
Google’s Genie 4 builds worlds you can walk through

Genie 4 builds a scene around you while you explore it

People, physics and sound now feel much closer to real life

Genie 4 is coming to paying subscribers first, and it still has rough edges

Type a line describing a quiet lake on a misty morning, with a man playing the saxophone on a small floating platform, and Google 's new AI will build that place for you. You can then move around it, glide the camera over the water and hear the saxophone as you go.This is Genie 4, the newest version of what Google calls a world model, unveiled by its research lab Google DeepMind on Tuesday. It is not open to the public yet, but a waitlist is already up, and the demos give a good sense of what it can do.Using it feels closer to playing a video game than watching a video. You start by typing a description or uploading a photo, and Genie 4 creates the scene on screen. Press the arrow keys to walk forward, turn around or move the camera, and it draws whatever lies in that direction, frame by frame, as you go.Unlike a game, nothing here was designed beforehand. There are no ready-made levels or characters waiting to be found, and everything you see is created the moment you look at it.You can also change the scene while you are in it. Type that you want it to start raining, ask for a different view or bring a new person into the frame, and the world adjusts without starting over. Behind the scenes, Google's Gemini AI makes sure these changes fit in naturally and that the place stays consistent as you move around.Each session can now run for around two minutes while staying consistent, roughly twice as long as the previous version, Genie 3.The biggest change from Genie 3 is how real everything looks. Objects move the way you would expect them to, so a falling maple seed spins on its way to the ground and things collide more convincingly.People are where you notice it most. Characters in the older version often moved stiffly, while those in Genie 4 walk naturally, react to what is around them and can be directed as the scene plays out. One of Google's examples is a crowded Japanese railway station from the 1980s, with passengers filling the platform and a long red train on the nearest track.Sound is new as well. Every scene now comes with its own audio, from waves on a beach to wind in the trees, and characters can speak. They chat with each other and respond to what you do or to whatever happens around them.A small group of testers has been putting all of this to use. Filmmakers are walking through scenes before shooting them, trying out camera angles, lighting and dialogue. Photographers are turning old photos into places you can step into, and game makers are testing ideas in minutes before writing a line of code. Google is also using it to let robots practise tasks in a simulated room before trying them in a real one.For now, only a small group of testers can use Genie 4. Google says it will reach AI Ultra subscribers in the coming weeks through Project Genie, its app for creating these worlds, along with developers who build apps on Google's AI. Ultra is the most expensive of Google's AI plans, and there is no word yet on whether the cheaper ones will get access later. Anyone interested can sign up for the waitlist on the Project Genie page.It is also clearly unfinished, and Google says as much. The longer you spend in a world, the more its details can drift, with objects changing shape or disappearing altogether. Sound does not always line up with what is on screen, and text such as signs or labels can come out hard to read.To keep its creations from being mistaken for real footage, every video and audio clip Genie 4 makes carries an invisible watermark that marks it as AI-generated.Typing a sentence and stepping into the place it describes is, at the moment, something only a handful of testers get to do, two minutes at a time. Google's plan is to widen that circle soon, starting with the people already paying for its top AI plan.
Article Summary: Genie 4 is coming to paying subscribers first, and it still has rough edges. Unlike a game, nothing here was designed beforehand. There are no ready-made levels or characters waiting to be found. Everything you see is created the moment you look at it.

Article Title: Roblox accused of scraping 145GB of 3D files for AI training, adult content included; 3D modelling site says: As far as our logs show, nobody…
Article Text:
(Image via: Roblox)

Update: This story has been updated with a statement from

Roblox

.

Original story follows

What happened

What Roblox has to say

Kids gaming platform Roblox has been accused of scrapping 145GB of 3D files for training artificial intelligence (AI). Independent 3D modeling community Open3DLab shared a blog post where it alleged that a crawler that “belonged to Roblox walked through almost every project on Open3DLab, SFMLab and SmutBase, and proceeded to download complete copies of 1,027 files from 712 projects. 145.5 GB of our creators' work, downloaded for what we assume are AI training purposes”. The crawler used trellis2-data-sourcing/1.0 (3D foundation model research; [redacted]@roblox.com) as its user agent, with the data coming from a single Amazon AWS address.“We want to be careful here. We don't think Roblox set out to collect adult content, and we have no evidence that any of it reached a model or a product. The scrapes were likely automated. But that is exactly the problem: as far as our logs show, nobody checked. A crawler working for a company whose platform tens of millions of children use was pointed at an adult site, and it took explicit models without telling them apart from anything else,” the blog post reads.On Sunday, 18th of October, Open3DLab says it noticed a crawler making a large number of requests to sites and download infrastructure. The crawler sent the same user agent on every request, trellis2-data-sourcing/1.0 (3D foundation model research; [redacted]@roblox.com).It came from a single Amazon Web Services (AWS) address. It had read the main page of 18,926 projects, which is practically the 3D modeling community’s entire catalogue, in 26,429 requests over a span of 34 hours.After pulling the project pages, it downloaded complete copies of 1,027 files from 712 projects, 145.5 GB in all, before suspending operations during the weekend. The downloads include 364 files (54.8 GB) from 224 projects on SmutBase, which hosts adult content only. With the SFMLab projects marked adult, 345 of the 712 projects (62.6 GB) are adult content.The main limiting factor in the number of files downloaded was the crawler's reliance on the free download servers, which have caps on speed limit and number of concurrent downloads. The crawler did not respect robots.txt, (which it did retrieve), ignored Terms of Service, (which forbid scraping), and defied the creators' licenses: 423 of the 712 projects are licensed for non-commercial use only. Within the sample it retrieved, it took adult projects at the same rate as everything else. Some examples include models of Eve from Stellar Blade, Mei from Overwatch, and a Horse cock dildo.The 3D lab says that after detecting the crawler on October 18, it “blocked further attempts the same morning”.Roblox reached out to TOI Tech with a statement.“A Roblox researcher built an agent to collect publicly available 3D assets that mistakenly scraped content from Open3DLab, failing to operate as intended. The agent was decommissioned and the data was not used for any purpose, including training any AI models. We are strengthening safeguards for how agents like this are built and reviewed, and will continue to do so as the agentic landscape evolves,” Roblox spokesperson told TOI Tech.
Article Summary: Roblox accused of scraping 145GB of 3D files for training artificial intelligence (AI) Independent 3D modeling community Open3DLab shared a blog post where it alleged that a crawler that ‘belonged to Roblox’ downloaded 1,027 files from 712 projects’ The downloads include 364 files from 224 projects on SmutBase, which hosts adult content only.

Article Title: IIT Kharagpur highlights success of Nagar Udyam initiative through campus pilot
Article Text: The Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Kharagpur has highlighted the success of its Nagar Udyam initiative that was launched as a pilot within the campus during Durga Puja this year.This is a pioneering solar-powered smart street vending initiative, conceptualised by Prof. Suman Chakraborty, Director, IIT Kharagpur, through its SETU Cloud Kitchen Connect.The aim is to popularise the concept among micro-entrepreneurs, allowing them to do business in a sustainable manner.This model allows a business to start without renting a shop, building permanent infrastructure or occupying roadside space after working hours.It enables an entrepreneur to take an entire business home at night and move it towards customers the next morning.Apart from Prof. Chakraborty, Siddharth Singh Dangi, SDPO, Kharagpur and several others, including small entrepreneurs, were present during the inauguration of the project. This is part of the institute's Platinum Jubilee commitment to translate design and technology into tangible social and economic opportunities.The project involves a small three-wheeled cart that can be towed by the owner's motorcycle. This will enable the entrepreneur to move to where there is demand. It has a range of about 30 km, subject to operational and road-safety validation.Once the day's business is done, the home-storage unit can be taken home, thereby clearing up public road space. The cart has solar-cum-battery renewal-energy-enabled essential low-power functions, with compact battery storage.The carts have the SETU digital backbone, including QR-enabled identification, cashless payments, training and pathways to financial inclusion. They also have built-in hygiene, with protected food display, food-grade surfaces and three-way waste segregation.Through the campus demonstration, IIT Kharagpur hopes to replicate the model across West Bengal, allowing street vendors to operate with dignity, without getting into trouble with the authorities.The compact vending structure can be towed by the owner behind a motorcycle, positioned at suitable places of concentrated demand and taken back home after business hours.A vendor could potentially cater to commuters in one part of the day and to a campus or community gathering later, without being tied to a costly permanent storefront. Its proposed mobility over roughly 30 kilometres offers a route to wider customer access.This changes the equation for both livelihoods and urban space. Rather than treating the entrepreneur’s business and pedestrian accessibility as competing priorities, the design aims for flexible, appropriately authorised vending that does not permanently claim a portion of the road.Further envisaged elements include food-safety status access, grievance redressal and data-assisted governance.“Our ambition is not simply to redesign a street cart; it is to redesign the opportunity around the person who runs it. A business that can move with demand, return home at night and connect to clean energy and digital finance can turn an opportunity seeker into a job creator. That is the kind of technology translation IIT Kharagpur stands for," Prof Chakraborty had said during the launch.The initiative suggests a fresh approach to public-space management: vending with clearer identification, better food practices, mobility and reduced permanent obstruction. These benefits will depend on practical traffic safeguards, lawful operating locations and coordination with civic authorities.As stated by Shri Siddharth Singh Dangi, SDPO, Kharagpur, “The best solutions for our streets must protect livelihoods as well as public safety. A mobile, identifiable and responsibly operated vending unit offers an interesting way to reduce permanent obstruction while preserving economic opportunity. The key will be disciplined implementation, safe movement and compliance with local rules.”The launch at the IIT Kharagpur campus evaluated food safety, operational efficiency, environmental performance, mobility, vendor experience and consumer response.Evidence from the pilot is intended to inform a prospective West Bengal Smart Street Vendor Framework, covering cart standards, food-safety practices, space management and measurable social outcomes. In this micro-startup vision, someone who cannot afford a permanent shop may still be able to build a business — and, over time, create jobs for others.
Article Summary: Nagar Udyam is a pioneering solar-powered smart street vending initiative. The aim is to popularise the concept among micro-entrepreneurs. This model allows a business to start without renting a shop, building permanent infrastructure or occupying roadside space after working hours.

Article Title: Canada's immigration authority to international students: You can only work in Canada if your study permit conditions says …
Article Text:
What the rules say

Study permit must allow work

Risk of losing student status

Consequences of working too many hours

Working after graduation

Watch for scams

Canada's immigration authority has issued a fresh reminder to international students, warning that they can work in the country only if their study permit explicitly allows it and that violating work conditions could have serious consequences, including the loss of student status and possible removal from Canada. In a recent post, Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) highlighted key rules that international students must follow while working during their studies. The agency said students can only work in Canada if the conditions listed on their study permit authorize them to work on or off campus. “Important information for international students who plan to work while studying:• You can only work in Canada as an international student if your study permit conditions say you can.• If you are eligible to work off campus, you can only work up to 24 hours per week while classes are in session.• Working more than you are allowed is a violation of your study permit conditions, which can have serious consequences,” wrote IRCC in a post on X (formerly known as Twitter).IRCC’s guidance says a student can work on or off campus only if the study permit lists a condition allowing it. The department tells students to pay close attention to the number of hours they are allowed to work off campus.A study permit is the document that sets out these terms, and holding one does not give automatic permission to take a job.The immigration department stated that international students are eligible to work in Canada only if their study permit contains a condition permitting on-campus or off-campus employment. Students have been advised to carefully review their permits before accepting any job. IRCC's social media post also reminded students that those eligible to work off campus can work a maximum of 24 hours per week while classes are in session. Working beyond the permitted limit constitutes a violation of study permit conditions.According to the agency, students who work more hours than allowed risk losing their student status. The department noted that non-compliance with permit conditions could also affect future applications for study permits or work permits. In some cases, individuals may be required to leave Canada. "Working more hours than you're allowed is a violation of your study permit conditions," IRCC said, adding that students could face consequences if they fail to follow the employment rules attached to their permits.According to IRCC’s page on unauthorized work, working more than the allowed hours breaches the study permit conditions. A student who does so can lose their student status, and future study or work permit applications may be refused. The student may also have to leave the country.The department’s wider warning about unauthorized work, which applies to anyone working in Canada without permission, lists further risks. These include removal from Canada, a permanent record of fraud with IRCC and a five-year ban on returning. Such a record can also hurt the chances of future applications being approved, including for permanent residence. IRCC also says people working without authorisation face greater risks of unsafe conditions, wage theft, abuse and forced or unpaid labour.IRCC says students who want to work after they graduate generally need a work permit, and some are eligible for a post-graduation work permit (PGWP). A graduate who has applied for a PGWP can work full-time while waiting for a decision, but only if certain conditions are met. The applicant must have held a valid study permit when applying, must have completed the program and must have been eligible to work off campus while studying without exceeding the allowed hours. Those who don’t meet these conditions must wait for their work permit before starting a new job.IRCC’s guidance for workers also lists warning signs of immigration fraud, which students may encounter when looking for jobs. These include anyone who promises a work permit or job offer in exchange for payment, asks for documents or payment through social media, or offers free room and board in return for work. IRCC says people who work legally are protected by Canada’s labour laws and can contact provincial or territorial labour standards offices without their employer’s permission.
Article Summary: Canada's immigration authority has issued a fresh reminder to international students. Students can only work in Canada if the conditions listed on their study permit authorize them to work on or off campus. Working more than the allowed hours breaches the study permit conditions. A student who does so can lose their student status and future study or work permit applications may be refused.

Article Title: In 1990, American billionaire Mark Cuban sold his software company MicroSolutions for $2 million, the first thing he dumped after that was ...
Article Text:
The watch came off the day Mark Cuban sold MicroSolutions

Mark Cuban: It was never just about becoming rich

The philosophy still shapes his habits

An attention-seeking kid from Pittsburgh

From MicroSolutions to Broadcast.com and the Mavericks

American billionaire Mark Cuban , best known today as the former majority owner of the Dallas Mavericks and a longtime investor on Shark Tank, has revealed that the first thing he got rid of after becoming a millionaire was not a possession he could not afford before, but the watch on his wrist. According to a Fortune report, Cuban said the decision reflected his desire to take control of his own time rather than live by someone else's schedule. Speaking on a recent episode of a podcast, Cuban said that on the day of the sale he took it off his watch and swore he would never wear one again, because wearing a watch meant working on someone else’s time. Fortune says he made about $2 million from the sale, which launched him on the path to major career success.Speaking on a recent episode of The Diary of a CEO podcast hosted by Steven Bartlett, Cuban recalled the moment he sold his software company MicroSolutions in 1990 and became a millionaire. “The day I sold MicroSolutions, I took off my watch and I said, ‘I’m never going to wear a watch again because that means I’m working on somebody else’s time,’” Cuban said.The entrepreneur reportedly made around $2 million personally from the sale, a milestone that marked the beginning of his journey toward becoming one of America's most successful self-made billionaires.While Cuban's net worth is now estimated at more than $10 billion, he said accumulating wealth was never the primary objective. Instead, his goal was achieving independence and having complete control over how he spent his time. “I just thought I hated being broke,” Cuban said on the podcast. “I wanted to control my own destiny. That was a big thing, and I wanted to be able to control my own time.”He contrasted his experience with that of his parents, who worked traditional jobs and were obligated to show up according to someone else's schedule. According to Cuban, financial success represented freedom rather than luxury. The idea of controlling his own time became one of the guiding principles behind many of his later business decisions.Although Cuban eventually softened his no-watch rule and now wears an Apple Watch for its health and fitness data, he said the thinking behind the gesture remains central to how he approaches life and business. The billionaire also explained why he avoids wearing ties, saying personal confidence comes from freedom and independence rather than formal dress codes.“Why I won’t wear a tie? Swag isn’t how you dress,” Cuban said. “Swag is being able to tell somebody else how they dress.” His preference for flexibility extends to communication as well. Cuban has previously said he favours emails over phone calls because they allow him to respond thoughtfully and save time. He has also spoken about avoiding unnecessary meetings, arguing that such habits free up hours in the day.Cuban’s drive started long before he had a fortune. He grew up in a working-class family outside Pittsburgh and told Bartlett he was the “fat kid” at school who would do almost anything for attention, including wearing a shirt with profanity on it and ripping a pair of jeans up to the hip and stapling them back together. Even so, most classmates did not remember him after he became famous, and someone once circled the wrong photo of him in his high school yearbook. He said that insecurity motivated him because he wanted to prove people wrong.At Indiana University, which he described as a fresh start, he covered his junior-year costs by running a chain letter from his dorm. After graduating he moved to Dallas and sold software until his boss fired him, which pushed him to start MicroSolutions.After the sale, Cuban did not reinvest the money. He said he did the exact opposite, buying a lifetime pass on American Airlines and travelling widely for fun. Much more money followed when he started Broadcast.com and sold it to Yahoo in 1999 for $5.7 billion in stock, which took his net worth past $1 billion. Cuban said that deal changed everything, because he no longer had to hustle and worry about what came next and could do whatever he wanted.That freedom let him buy the Dallas Mavericks in 2000 for $285 million, something he said he never imagined. He sold his majority stake in late 2023 in a deal Fortune puts at $3.5 billion. Today he is focused on Mark Cuban Cost Plus Drugs, which he started in 2022. The company sells generic and select brand-name prescription drugs directly to consumers and health care providers, cutting out pharmacy benefit managers, which tend to inflate retail drug prices.
Article Summary: Mark Cuban sold his software company MicroSolutions in 1990 and became a millionaire. On the day of the sale he took it off his watch and swore he would never wear one again. Cuban said the decision reflected his desire to take control of his own time rather than live by someone else's schedule. The entrepreneur reportedly made around $2 million personally from the sale.

Article Title: Google, Meta and other tech companies resist ICE demands for user data amid US government immigration crackdown
Article Text:
Google, Meta and other tech companies resist ICE demands for user data amid US government immigration crackdown

Tech Giants getting caught between legal fights and retaliation

Tech giants, including Google and Meta, are reportedly resisting the Trump administration as federal immigration authorities escalate their use of subpoenas to track down online critics. Silicon Valley companies are delaying responses, challenging broad government requests and expanding notification policies for their users, as per a report by The Wall Street Journal. The pushback comes as tech executives brace for potential congressional investigations led by Democrats following upcoming midterm elections, while balancing privacy concerns from their own workforces and navigating relations with the current administration. Lawmakers are already pressing these companies to explain why sensitive customer details have been turned over to federal authorities.“They need to be prepared to say, under oath, why they did what they did,” said Rep. Shri Thanedar, who co-launched a probe into tech compliance earlier this year. Over the past year, Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), a division of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), has monitored platforms, including YouTube, Facebook, Instagram, Reddit, TikTok and X it classifies as threats to agents or enforcement activities.To pull user records, federal authorities have turned heavily to administrative subpoenas. Unlike judicial warrants or grand jury subpoenas, these orders are written and approved directly by ICE officials without prior judicial review – a practice former officials from both major political parties describe as a sharp departure from standard procedure.The report also highlights the volume of government requests. For example, Google logged approximately 28,600 US government subpoenas between January and June 2025, matching similar numbers through the remainder of that year. To counter resistance, DHS has teamed with the Department of Justice in recent weeks to issue grand jury subpoenas, which carry higher legal penalties for noncompliance.Meta reported handing over at least some data in 88.8% of US government requests received between July and December of last year.Both Google and Meta executives have privately voiced concerns over their exposure. Inside Meta, leadership is assessing vulnerabilities to Democratic oversight if congressional power changes hands. Google leadership has weighed similar concerns, while worrying that stonewalling could trigger retaliation from the administration, such as further scrutiny of its pending federal antitrust cases.In response, Google pointed to its operational safeguards, noting its processes are built to guard customer privacy while satisfying legal requirements, emphasising that it rejects demands deemed overbroad.Federal authorities maintain their actions adhere to the law. An ICE spokesperson stated that operations are “conducted in accordance with applicable law and policy.”
Article Summary: Google, Meta and other tech companies resist ICE demands for user data amid US government immigration crackdown. Tech giants getting caught between legal fights and retaliation. Lawmakers are already pressing these companies to explain why sensitive customer details have been turned over to federal authorities.

Article Title: Likely for the first time ever, Elon Musk shares the 'whole schedule' on how he spends time with his 14 children; says: I see my kids with …
Article Text:
Elon Musk shares the 'whole schedule' on how he spends time with his 14 children

Elon Musk has 14 children with four women

Elon Musk, probably for the first time, has shared the “whole schedule” about how he co-parent his 14 children. An X (formerly Twitter) post recently claimed that Musk's “co parenting arrangements” are “managed through a system that former staff have described as closer to corporate scheduling than family life”. The tech billionaire rebutted the claim stating that his five kids are “adults and live independent lives”. Elon Musk further revealed that he keeps seeing his kids regularly. Musk shared that he sees his kids with Claire ‘every other week’ and kids with Shivon Zillis every few days.“Nannies coordinate with assistants. Assistants coordinate with each other. Calendar invites determine which children see their father on which days. The man who has 14 children with 4 women manages his fatherhood the way he manages his companies: through delegation, scheduling, and process,” X user Space Tourist @spacetourist0 claimed in the post.“The children within each household are grouped. The five with Justine are one unit. The three with Grimes are another. The three with Shivon are another. The child with the mother who has not been publicly identified is another.Each unit has its own schedule, its own nanny team, and its own relationship to the central calendar. The units do not frequently interact with each other despite sharing a father. The half siblings exist in parallel rather than in community,” the post alleged.Replying to the post, Elon Musk clarified “This is wrong on many levels. My older 5 children are adults and live independent lives.”“I see my kids with Claire every other week and kids with Shivon every few days. That’s the whole schedule,” Musk further stated.Elon Musk has 14 publicly known children with four women: his first wife, Canadian author Justine Wilson; musician Grimes, whose real name is Claire Boucher; Neuralink executive Shivon Zilis; and conservative influencer and author Ashley St. Clair. Musk and Wilson had six children, including their first son, Nevada, who died at 10 weeks old.He has three children with Grimes, four with Zilis and one son, Romulus, with St. Clair. His children include twins and triplets, and some of their names have drawn public attention because of their unusual spellings.
Article Summary: Elon Musk has 14 publicly known children with four women: his first wife, Canadian author Justine Wilson; musician Grimes, whose real name is Claire Boucher; Neuralink executive Shivon Zilis; and conservative influencer and author Ashley St. Clair. His children include twins and triplets, and some of their names have drawn public attention because of their unusual spellings. The tech billionaire rebutted the claim stating that his five kids are ‘adults and live independent lives’

Article Title: Swiss tech company Proton says 2026 is its last year of hiring engineers; CEO tells employees: Next year we hire what we used to call...
Article Text:
Proton now writes 90% of its code with AI, says CTO

Proton staff face AI re-interviews that could cost them their jobs

Proton, the Swiss company behind the encrypted email service Proton Mail, may stop hiring software engineers altogether after this year. CEO Andy Yen told staff in an internal Slack message that 2026 "will be the last year that we hire engineers. " From next year, he wrote, the company will instead hire "what we used to call product managers, to build things with AI."Yen made the remarks in the company's security channel in late August, according to 404 Media, which spoke to eight current and one former employee and reviewed internal Slack chats and meeting audio. In the same message, he predicted that by the end of the year most developers would stop programming and start writing specs for tests that AI would code and run. Proton is now preparing to re-interview staff about their AI use, and has warned that the outcome could decide who keeps their job.The shift is already visible in the codebase. Chief technology officer Bart Butler said in a meeting that about 90% of the company's code in October was written by AI, according to audio obtained by 404 Media. Several employees said much of it is produced with Anthropic's Claude, which Yen also tells staff to use.Butler followed up with a self-described AI manifesto, posted on Slack on a Friday afternoon. It told engineers their "old job is gone" and said most code at Proton should eventually be reviewed by AI rather than humans. Falling behind on AI, it argued, was an existential threat to the company's mission.It has also set up an email address for staff to flag anything blocking AI adoption, and installed software that tracks how much code AI is writing.Some engineers have pushed back on security. When one employee suggested taking a few days to pentest new code before it went live, Yen called the idea "loser thinking" and told the team to "stop lovingly handcrafting all our code and use AI more." Another engineer warned that AI would not fix things on its own, since security sat low on the company's list of priorities.On Monday, Proton emailed employees to say it would re-interview staff across the company between November 4 and 11. "These re-interviews are consequential," the email read, adding that the assessments could lead to changes in roles, responsibilities and continued employment. Interviewers will come from outside the employee's own team and reporting line. Yen had already interviewed more than 40 senior leaders across engineering and product.An internal document seen by 404 Media points to a commercial angle. It says the company is not on track to meet its annual recurring revenue target this year "due to insufficient velocity," and describes Proton as underperforming by every metric that matters. Yen, though, told a senior employee in Slack that if he believed the move was financially driven and didn't trust Yen's word otherwise, Proton "might not be the place for you. "The Swiss firm did not dispute 404 Media's reporting. A spokesperson acknowledged that some staff are unhappy with the company's direction and many are anxious, adding that leadership had sometimes been "too blunt or too slow in explaining ourselves."In public, Yen has pitched Proton's AI work, including its Lumo chatbot, as a privacy-first answer to Big Tech. Inside the company, the November interviews will show what his "last year" of engineering hires means for the ones already there.
Article Summary: Proton, the company behind Proton Mail, may stop hiring software engineers. CEO Andy Yen told staff in an internal Slack message that 2026 "will be the last year that we hire engineers" Proton is now preparing to re-interview staff about their AI use. The outcome could decide who keeps their job.

Article Title: After ‘hitting’ RAM supply, AI demand may have triggered another key component shortage for PC makers
Article Text:
AI-generated image

Silicon giants lock up capacity

Raw materials and factory tooling hit a wall

Acute talent shortage another big reason

First it was memory chips (RAM) and processors, now, the boom in artificial intelligence (AI) computing is squeezing another foundational piece of hardware: printed circuit boards (PCBs) and chip substrates. As PC makers like HP and Dell map out their hardware supply needs for 2027, this once-overlooked part of the electronics chain has suddenly turned into a major roadblock. According to a report by Nikkei Asia, industry managers say factory lines worldwide are pivoting toward high-margin AI infrastructure, leaving traditional consumer electronics, including laptops and smartphones, scrambling for capacity.“Various types of PCBs have become a critical bottleneck in our product planning for next year. Even though PC shipments could decline again next year, we are still struggling to secure enough PCB supplies to meet our needs,” a manager at an American PC maker told Nikkei Asia on the condition of anonymity.PCBs and chip substrates are a crucial part and are the wiring backbone inside nearly every electronic product. They let chips talk to one another and shape overall system performance. They have been viewed as a low-cost, low-profile part of the bill of materials compared to advanced silicon but now have become vital to keeping data moving quickly and managing heat in AI clusters.“Everyone is shifting production capacity toward AI-related products, leaving traditional PCB demand from consumer electronics and notebooks increasingly underserved. Meanwhile, the shortage is not only associated with PCBs but also with materials to build PCBs,” said a PCB industry manager supplying Nvidia, Intel, and Google.The shift has created a severe ripple effect through upstream suppliers. S.C. Chien, chairman of key supplier Unimicron, pointed out that AI and high-speed networking chips need larger substrates with more layers, denser interconnects, and tighter heat dissipation standards. Meeting those specs demands specialised manufacturing machinery that is increasingly hard to get, the report said.According to Chien, about 20% of the equipment required to produce advanced substrates and PCBs now has lead times twice as long as before, with some tools facing delivery delays of up to 30 months.Basic build materials are under similar pressure. For example, Copper Clad Laminate (CCL) costs have surged at least 12 times since July; glass fabrics, which are used in everyday consumer devices, are drying up as textile mills switch production to low-Dk and low-Df glass suited for AI servers. This has led to a growing queue that one sales representative said new orders placed today cannot be delivered until late 2028.The report highlighted that the crunch was evident at Taiwan's annual PCB trade show this month, where procurement teams from Apple, Qualcomm and HP gathered to negotiate directly with equipment and material vendors.Beyond hardware, the sector faces an acute talent shortage. Average salaries across the PCB industry have climbed 20% to 30%, the report noted, citing human resources consultants. Specialists in AI server boards, high-end quality control and technical sales are commanding pay packages roughly double their prior earnings.
Article Summary: PCBs and chip substrates are a crucial part and are the wiring backbone inside nearly every electronic product. The shift has created a severe ripple effect through upstream suppliers. Average salaries across the PCB industry have climbed 20% to 30%, the report noted.

Article Title: Spotify considers AI remix feature for up to $5 extra a month; secures Universal deal as Sony talks continue
Article Text:
Representative Image

What subscribers would be able to create

Why label deals do not guarantee artists’ participation

“I would never,”

“Absolutely no. Hard line on that.”

How artists could earn from fan-made remixes

“If one of your fans creates the remix of your song, that actually increases the share of the streaming [revenue] pool that you get,”

Spotify is considering an extra charge for AI remixes. The streaming company is targeting an early 2027 launch for a service that would let paying subscribers create remixes and covers of existing songs, according to the Financial Times. It is weighing an additional monthly fee of $4 to $5, though it has not finalised either the pricing or the launch date.Spotify has secured licensing agreements with Universal Music Group, Merlin and Believe, while negotiations with Sony Music and Warner Music continue. The company is also seeking participation from individual artists, which would remain optional even if their labels have signed agreements. The proposed service could create another source of subscription revenue while directing royalties from fan-made versions back to the original artists.The service would let listeners change existing music with AI, such as turning a folk song into a dance track or making one participating artist appear to cover another’s song.That approach differs from services such as Suno, which generate new songs from text prompts. Spotify’s product would use music from artists who have agreed to participate.According to people familiar with the plans cited by the FT, Spotify is aiming for a first-quarter launch, potentially around February’s Grammy Awards.The timetable remains subject to change, and Spotify declined to comment.The company announced the product in May. In August, co-chief executive Gustav Söderström told investors it would launch when ready.Spotify and Universal have been meeting individual artists to persuade them to make their music available, the report said. Securing participation from major contemporary stars has proved harder than winning support from some established older performers, according to one person familiar with the discussions. Universal artist Olivia Rodrigo opposed using AI in her music during an interview with the Hollywood Reporter.she said.Artists would retain the choice to decline regardless of their record label’s licensing agreement with Spotify.Under the proposed arrangement, royalties from remixes would flow to the original artists. Spotify is also developing a system that would let these versions appear in playlists, with their streams counting toward the original songs in its music charts.At a September investor conference, Söderström argued that fan-created versions could give older artists another way to earn from their catalogues.he said.The service forms part of Spotify’s effort to generate more revenue from subscribers. Bernstein analyst Ian Moore estimates that 7% to 8% of its US subscribers could sign up by the end of 2028.
Article Summary: Spotify is targeting an early 2027 launch for a service that would let paying subscribers create remixes and covers of existing songs. It is weighing an additional monthly fee of $4 to $5, though it has not finalised either the pricing or the launch date.

Article Title: Performance remained strong: SAP CFO Dominik Asam on why company is switching to cheaper AI models from Google, OpenAI and Anthropic
Article Text:
Image credit: X (Twitter)

Why cheaper models matter for SAP

“The goal is healthy margins as scale grows, not an absolute reduction in AI expenditure,”

SAP is replacing some expensive AI models with cheaper alternatives. Chief financial officer Dominik Asam told Reuters that the company has made substitutions in products, including its internal consulting assistant, where lower-cost models could still deliver the required performance. The move is expected to help generate more than €2 billion in AI-driven efficiency gains.Asam told Reuters that performance remained strong after some of the replacements. SAP uses more than 70 AI models from providers including Google, OpenAI and Anthropic, and increasingly selects the cheapest option that meets its standards. However, the company expects its overall AI spending to rise as adoption grows, with the changes intended to support profitability as usage expands.SAP’s pricing model makes the cost of running AI tasks relevant to its profit margins. Unlike many AI providers, SAP charges customers for completed tasks rather than the computing resources used to produce responses. Reducing the underlying cost of completing those tasks can therefore help the company retain more of the revenue.SAP said in answers to Reuters’ questions.The company is replacing selected models where cheaper alternatives meet performance requirements. The report does not identify which individual models were removed or name their replacements.Cost and performance are not the only considerations shaping SAP’s AI decisions. Asam said government agencies and companies in regulated industries increasingly specify requirements for AI models and exclude some options based on their origin. European customers are also increasingly asking for local solutions.
Article Summary: SAP is replacing some expensive AI models with cheaper alternatives. The move is expected to help generate more than €2 billion in AI-driven efficiency gains. SAP uses more than 70 AI models from providers including Google, OpenAI and Anthropic. The company expects its overall AI spending to rise as adoption grows.

Halloween is a holiday celebrated each year on October 31, mixing ancient harvest and religious customs with modern fun. Article Title: Days after getting the largest settlement involving food employees in New York history, Mayor Zohran Mamdani is upset with DoorDash for spending $17 billion on rival Instacart; warns New Yorkers about
Article Text:
What is Doordash's $131 million-plus settlement with New York City

What DoorDash said on settlement with New York City

In a long statement DoorDash announced that it has reached a settlement with New York City's Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) over compliance with the pay rules for delivery workers. Below is the full statement from the company:

New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani is not happy with delivery platform DoorDash's spending $17 billion to buy rival Instacart. And he made it clear in a post online. Mamdani's dismay comes almost a month after he managed to win $131.5 million from DoorDash for delivery workers in New York. In September, Mayor Mamdani announced a historic $131.5 million enforcement action against DoorDash for systematic violations of New York City's Delivery Worker Laws. The deal has been termed as the largest worker settlement in New York City history and the largest settlement involving food delivery workers in the United States.Slamming the Doordash deal, Mamdani wrote, "Just last month, DoorDash couldn’t seem to find the money to pay their deliveristas — until our administration forced them to give back $131M+ in stolen wages and penalties. This week, they’ve managed to find $17 billion to acquire one of their main competitors. Corporate consolidation means higher prices, harsher exploitation, and greater economic inequality for New Yorkers. We’ve stood up to these giants before. That doesn’t stop now."DoorDash is offering $17 billion to buy Instacart in a deal that could consolidate the grocery delivery business in the US and abroad. The companies say the tie-up would combine DoorDash’s global reach and expertise in logistics with Instacart’s purpose-built technology and long relationships with grocers.It could also help the companies better compete with rivals like Amazon.In September this year, Mayor Zohran Kwame Mamdani, Deputy Mayor for Economic Justice Julie Su and Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) Commissioner Samuel AA Levine announced $131.5 million enforcement action against DoorDash for what they called systematic violations of New York City's Delivery Worker Laws. “When a worker earns a wage, they deserve to be paid that wage — not tomorrow, not after a lawsuit, but on time and in full,” Mayor Zohran Kwame Mamdani had said. He added, “DoorDash underpaid more than 260,000 workers, and today we are getting that money back. This is what it looks like when City government stands with working people: We find the violations, we enforce the law and we make sure workers get what they’re owed. No corporation is above the law, and this administration will keep fighting until every worker gets the pay and protections they deserve.”Simply put, we screwed up. Our mistakes meant some Dashers were underpaid or paid late. While these mistakes weren’t intentional, that doesn’t make them okay. We pride ourselves on operational excellence at DoorDash – and this was not excellent, nor was it acceptable. Dashers should be paid in full, on time, every time. We are sorry to the Dashers we let down.We’re making things right by paying every impacted Dasher what they are owed and fixing what caused this so it doesn’t happen again. The $131.5 million settlement with the City includes $12.3 million for Dashers who were underpaid or paid late and over $83 million to resolve a disagreement over how to calculate pay for time Dashers spend online between deliveries. DCWP is receiving $16.7 million in fines owed to them as part of the settlement.What went wrong with Dasher payments?New York City has the most complex earning standard for delivery workers in the country. Since it took effect in 2023, New York City Dashers have earned more than $1 billion and the average Dasher pay per active hour before tips is roughly $30.Despite our best efforts to comply with the new rules, we made mistakes. Many errors were caused by technical bugs or happened in complicated situations: deliveries that crossed city boundaries, had multiple pickup or drop-off locations, or were only partially fulfilled or cancelled. In other cases, errors stemmed from Dashers providing incomplete or inaccurate banking information.Approximately 264,000 Dashers will receive a payment, including 209,000 for missing or late payments. Less than 1% of all payments to NYC Dashers were affected. Around $6.6 million worth of payments never reached Dashers, and another $5.7 million arrived days or in some cases, weeks late. The average missing payment owed to Dashers is $7.70, and 65% of impacted Dashers were underpaid by $1 or less, and the median payment will be around $48.What is on-call or online time?Most of this settlement isn't about late or missing pay, but how to calculate bonuses paid to Dashers for online or on-call time — the hours a Dasher is logged into the app but not on an active delivery. Under the City’s rules, Dashers must be paid for this time spent online between deliveries, and they were. We calculated on-call time differently than the City, and believe our approach was fair, practical, and legal. But rather than spend years fighting over whose method was right, we chose to pay Dashers sooner and use the City’s method going forward.What we're doing about itWe’re paying every impacted Dasher what they earned, and all affected Dashers will be contacted to be made whole in the coming weeks. Dashers will be paid a minimum of $10, even if they were underpaid by less than that.We’ve fixed the technical issues that caused these errors, including better validation of banking information to ensure we catch issues before it causes a missed payment, and we’ve strengthened our compliance program to help prevent this from happening again.This settlement reflects the responsibility we take for falling short. We’ve been working to finalize this for some time and already set aside the full amount in prior quarters.If you have additional questions about our settlement and whether you have been impacted, visit our Help Center here.
Article Summary: DoorDash announced that it has reached a settlement with New York City's Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) over compliance with the pay rules for delivery workers. In September, Mayor Zohran Kwame Mamdani announced a historic $131.5 million enforcement action against DoorDash for systematic violations of the Delivery Worker Laws.
